title: Insecure TLS flag is not applied to fetchMetrics, causing benchmark aborts against HTTPS targets
test: tests/benchmarkRuntime.test.js: 'metrics fetch against an HTTPS target with a self-signed certificate succeeds with allowInsecureTls' (plus the three companion tests in that file)
proof: Before the fix, the defect was shown by a standalone script: global fetch against a local HTTPS server with a self-signed certificate fails with DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT, and the benchmark had no way to pass the flag to it. The new test file failed on the unchanged code because scripts/runtime-metrics-client.js did not exist (MODULE_NOT_FOUND), so the test failed for a reason other than the certificate error. After the fix, scripts/runtime-metrics-client.js createMetricsFetcher uses node:https with rejectUnauthorized: !allowInsecureTls for https targets, and scripts/benchmark-runtime.js uses it for every /api/metrics request. The four tests in tests/benchmarkRuntime.test.js pass (self-signed with flag succeeds, self-signed without flag rejects, HTTP unaffected, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED unchanged).
